questions.answer: A set is an unordered, mutable collection of unique hashable elements backed by a hash table. Uniqueness auto-dedups; unordered means no indexing/slicing; mutable means add/remove. Hash-table gives O(1) average membership vs O(n) scan for lists.
questions.question: What are the three defining properties of a Python set, and why is a set faster than a list for membership checks?

questions.answer: `|` returns all elements from both; `&` only common; `-` elements in left but not right (directional); `^` elements in either but not both.
questions.question: State what each of `A | B`, `A & B`, `A - B`, `A ^ B` returns for A={1,2,3}, B={2,3,4}.

questions.answer: Use remove() when absence is a bug you want surfaced (KeyError). Use discard() for idempotent cleanup where absence is fine. pop() removes and returns an arbitrary element with no index argument; clear() empties to set().

questions.answer: `{}` creates an empty dict, not a set. Empty set is `set()`. So `type(x)` is dict and `.add` fails with AttributeError.

questions.answer: No. `pop()` takes no arguments and removes an arbitrary element since sets have no order/index. Use `discard(v)` to remove a specific value, or convert to sorted list to remove deterministically.
